summary: Iteration 159 backend-only verification of the users.setting_id/team_id derive-at-write refactor (Option B) in routers/org.py. Ran the pre-existing standalone regression (test_setting_id_sync_iter159.py — 4/4 assertions pass) plus authored a new API-level e2e suite (test_iter159_api_e2e.py — 7/7 pass, ~109s) that hits the live FastAPI endpoints as admin@supervision.com and verifies the resulting DB rows via direct asyncpg join against teams.setting_id. Both real bugfixes verified end-to-end: (1) update_team now clears BOTH team_id AND setting_id for the OLD supervisor when replaced/removed, AND the `if row['team_id'] == team_id` guard prevents clobbering an old supervisor who was reassigned elsewhere in the interim; (2) delete_team now nulls BOTH columns for every former member and they correctly appear in /api/org/structure's unassigned_users. All refactored-but-unchanged-behaviour paths (create_team+supervisor, add_member, assign-team both branches) still derive setting_id correctly from teams.setting_id with no drift, and RBAC 404/scope checks still fire (verified via bogus user/team IDs returning 404 not 500). No frontend changes were made and no smoke UI check was needed since this is purely a DB-write-path fix.
critical_code_review_comments: The `if row and row['team_id'] == team_id` guard in update_team (line 447) correctly avoids clobbering, but there is a subtle TOCTOU window: between the SELECT and the UPDATE the row could be moved by another concurrent request. In practice acceptable given the low contention on admin-only org mutations, but worth a comment or a single UPDATE ... WHERE team_id=$X form for defence-in-depth.

_sync_user_team uses UPDATE users SET team_id=$1, setting_id=$2 WHERE id=$3 without any org_id/tenant guard. All callers do org-scoped lookups first so it's fine today, but the helper itself is a footgun for future callers — consider adding AND org_id=$4 as a defence-in-depth check, or at least a docstring warning that callers own tenant scoping.

remove_member (line 506) still uses raw SQL rather than _sync_user_team, which is documented in the change note. Consistent for now, but a future consolidation pass could route it through the helper for uniformity.
test_credentials: admin@supervision.com / Admin123!X (used for all API calls)
seed_data_creation: All test data is per-test throwaway: org_settings + teams + users created with 'Iter159 API' name prefix and cleaned up in each test's finally block via asyncpg. No persistent seed data left behind. Verified with SELECT count on Iter159-prefixed rows post-run.
context_for_next_testing_agent: iter159 refactor of users.setting_id/team_id write path in routers/org.py is fully verified. The new _sync_user_team helper is drift-proof (setting_id always derived from teams.setting_id at write time). Both real bugfixes (update_team old-supervisor clear, delete_team member setting_id clear) work end-to-end with correct guards. Reusable regression suites: /app/backend/tests/test_setting_id_sync_iter159.py (standalone) and /app/backend/tests/test_iter159_api_e2e.py (pytest, 7 tests, hits public REACT_APP_BACKEND_URL). No open issues.
